narrative: OMX30 enters Wednesday in a technical straitjacket: bull market structure intact (+5.6% vs 200-MA) but conviction severely compromised by ADX at 16.8 (weak trend). Global cross-currents leave us directionless—European weakness (-0.32% to -0.60%), US flat, Asia strength (+1.94% Nikkei), and zero net correlation bias (-0.006%). Oil's dramatic 4.9% sell-off is a material headwind for industrials (28% of index) offsetting copper's modest +1.2% pop. RSI at 57 is true neutral, MACD above signal offers only marginal bullish lean, and we're already 1.3% from the 52W high with limited runway. The index sits 94% through its 52-week range—a crowded positioning signal.
morningBrief: OMX30 setup is agnostic. Technically we're still in a bull regime (+5.6% above 200-MA), MACD above signal, but ADX at 16.8 is limp—apply 30% confidence haircut per rules. Oil's -4.9% dump is the session's most important datapoint: expect industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo, Sandvik) to open softer on input cost anxiety. Copper +1.2% and gold +0.75% are minor tailwinds for Boliden but insufficient to offset broad malaise. Banks are mixed: yields up 29bp but EUR/SEK only +0.06% (muted). Watch the open for institutional reaction to overnight UK political noise (Burnham/NHS debate). Key support at 3085 (lower Bollinger), resistance at 3180 (50-MA). US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET is your only real macro catalyst today. Risk-off is lurking (VIX +1.12%) but not yet confirmed.
